doc.title: Dick Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006

title: John Ibach and replacements in the All-Stars
summary: Sherman remembers pianist and surgeon John Ibach, Dr. Jazz of Jacksonville, and notes Bill Semple replaced Emerson Brown.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Yeah. A very interesting guy. Tell me about John Ibach a little bit.

John Ibach was a beloved member of our band. I served on the Student Council with him as an undergraduate. He was a very fervent player, very passionate about it. And he has done a lot for jazz piano in Florida, he was known as Dr. Jazz in Jacksonville, and he sponsored some Marian McPartland concerts. He was well known by professionals and by audiences. But we loved him. He was a funny guy. And a dear man, a truly kind man. And we really missed him. I saw him a couple of times down in Florida when he was starting to get ill and it was cruel because his mind was so good. He was an extremely intelligent man, a great surgeon. So I miss him. That’s all I can say about him.
Do you see replacements in line for the All-Stars?

I don’t. But you never can tell. Now Bill Semple is the class of ’68. When Emerson Brown was starting to falter a bit, up steps Bill Semple and I get this guy. And he’s a guy © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-
from ’68 replacing a guy from ’56. So it’s always possible. I hope they will, I hope they’ll find them.
